newsitem.title: USA: Ralston's ex-wife says his decision a loss.
newsitem.headline: Ralston's ex-wife says his decision a loss.

text.p: The former wife of Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston said Tuesday his decision to withdraw from consideration to become chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff was a loss.

"I'm sorry because I know it will be a loss for him, and the military," Linda Ralston, 54, said in an interview in the Lexington Herald-Leader. Ralston took his name out of consideration Monday in the midst of a controversy over an adulterous affair he had 13 years ago -- after he had separated from Linda Ralston. Their divorce was final in 1988.

"I think we all make our own mistakes in life but it's what we do with them after that, and how we change, that I think really should matter," Linda Ralston said. She was interviewed in Somerset, Kentucky, where she grew up and now cares for her mother, the newspaper said.

She told the newspaper her former husband "without question" should have been the nominee for the top military post and was the most qualified person for the job. "My feeling is that it happened so long ago and that the general and I had already settled our differences," she said.
